text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Parliament is expected next week to pass legislation demanding higher bonds from travel agents and increasing regulation of the industry.
--Left and right wing politicians are seeking to regulate Tele Denmark's sale of subscriber information to other companies.

--Despite the generally buoyant stock market, the flow of new flotations is drying up due to a negative image created by market scandals and the experiences of companies who, despite an apparently succesful launch, did not see their shares perform as expected thereafter. relating to the case.
--Danish oil exports are expected to increase foreign currency earnings by 12-15 billion crowns in 1998, strengthening the national balance of payments.

--The government is still considering an early but mild increase to existing fiscal tightening. It has discussed with the left the possibilities of higher "green taxes" on cars and fuel and increasing employers' gross tax.

--Insurance companies Tryg-Baltica, Alm.Brand and Codan are co-ordinating their position on whether to sue Den Danske Bank for losses incurred in its sale to them of shares in Hafnia insurance shortly before its collapes in 1992.

--Unibank is raising interest from today on savings acounts where customers give six months notice of withdrawal but competitors do not intend to follow suit.A banking analyst said that the Unibank hike was primarily an advertising exercise and only 1.5 percent of its customers would gain any benefit.
--The government's plan to reduce the national debt, while cutting taxes and improving education and the environment is a fine aim but it does not have the resources to achieve it.
--Danish manufacturers, among them Cheminova, are exporting to Latin America pesticides banned at home for a decade.
